linguistic_propositions.proposition: A present-time equative assertion is formed by placing the two nominal elements side by side; the linking relation is structural and has no lexical exponent.
The element leaned upon fills the topic slot of the noun-initial sentence and the leaning element fills the comment slot.
The topic element is normally definite and the comment element normally indefinite.
A definite nominal followed by an indefinite nominal or adjective constitutes a complete assertion, while definite followed by definite is only a noun phrase.
Reversing the two elements alters meaning or emphasis rather than being free variation.
The term for predication is derived from a root meaning to lean or support, which motivates the topic/comment metaphor.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A sentence beginning with a noun is nominal and one beginning with a verb is verbal.
Both the topic and the comment of a noun-initial sentence carry nominative case.
Nominative is exponed by ḍamma on definite nominals and by nunated ḍamma on indefinite ones.
The topic is almost always definite because one cannot make a statement about an unidentified entity.
The comment is typically indefinite because a definite comment would yield an attributive phrase instead of an assertion.
The comment must match the topic in gender and in number.
Comment-before-topic orders exist and are governed by rules deferred to later study.
A comment may be realised as a single word, as a clause, or as a preposition or adverb phrase.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A comment realised by one word may be either an adjective describing the topic or a noun classifying it.
The single-word comment is nominative without exception.
Nominative on the comment is exponed by ḍamma, nunated ḍamma, the sound masculine plural ending, or the sound feminine plural ending.
A topic that is a plural of non-human referents takes feminine singular agreement in the comment.
Feminine agreement is realised by adding the feminine ending to the masculine base.
A defective (final-weak) adjective in the comment slot is nominative even though its ending is not overtly nominative on the surface.
Clause comments and phrase comments are not single-word comments and are excluded from this category.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A comment may be realised by a preposition-headed phrase or by a locative adverb phrase.
A nominal governed by a preposition is genitive.
A nominal following a locative adverb is genitive in the same way as after a preposition.
The phrase itself occupies the comment slot of the sentence.
Possession is expressed by the locative-accompaniment preposition or by the dative-like prefixed preposition.
The distinguishing test between the two comment realisations is that one word describes a quality while a phrase locates or attributes possession.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A sentence opening with a verb is verbal; its agent follows the verb and is nominative.
A verb preceding a plural agent stays singular and agrees only in gender.
When a nominal precedes the verb, the structure is a topic with a clausal comment, and the verb then agrees in number as well as gender.
The past-tense feminine exponent is a quiescent tāʾ whose vowel shifts to kasra before a following cluster for ease of articulation.
The object of the verb follows the agent and is accusative.
Sentence type is decided by the word class of the first word.
A broken plural of non-human referents controls the feminine verb form.
The verbal framing foregrounds the action while the nominal framing foregrounds the entity.

instructional_purpose: Treats definiteness as a system in its own right: it separates definite from indefinite nominals, enumerates the sources from which definiteness comes, names the surface markers, and connects the distinction back to the default definiteness of the two slots of the noun-initial sentence.
concepts_taught: the definite/indefinite partition of nominals
the definite article as one source of definiteness
nunation and the absence of the article as indefiniteness markers
six enumerated sources of definiteness: article, proper name, pronoun, demonstrative, relative noun, and annexation to a definite
definiteness inherited through annexation, including annexation to a pronominal suffix
the default pairing of a definite topic with an indefinite comment
the semantic contrast between specific and non-specific reference

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Every nominal is either definite or indefinite.
Indefiniteness is signalled by absence of the article together with the presence of nunation.
There are exactly six sources of definiteness.
A nominal annexed to a definite nominal, including a pronominal suffix, is itself definite.
In a noun-initial sentence the topic is normally definite and the comment normally indefinite.
If both slots were definite, a copula or a different construction would be required.
Definiteness changes reference from any member of a class to a specific known member.

recognition_criteria: presence of the definite article on the nominal
nunation on the ending, in the absence of any other definiteness source
membership in a closed class (pronoun, demonstrative, relative noun)
status as a proper name
being the first term of an annexation whose second term is definite
procedures: check the nominal against each definiteness source in turn
if none applies, classify the nominal as indefinite
when constructing a noun-initial sentence, select a definite topic and an indefinite comment
convert an indefinite nominal to definite by prefixing the article or by annexing it to a definite

indefinite topics licensed by specification, and definite comments, are excluded rather than explained

common_mistakes.pattern: reading any nunated nominal as indefinite
common_mistakes.why_wrong: proper names are definite yet nunated, so nunation is not a reliable indefiniteness test
common_mistakes.correction_principle: check the definiteness sources first and use nunation only as corroboration on common nouns

common_mistakes.pattern: reading any nominal without the article as indefinite
common_mistakes.why_wrong: annexed nominals, proper names, pronouns, demonstratives, and relative nouns are all definite without the article
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat the article as one source among several rather than as the definition of definiteness

common_mistakes.pattern: overlooking a pronominal suffix as a source of definiteness on its host
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the host of a pronominal suffix is the first term of an annexation to a definite and inherits definiteness
common_mistakes.correction_principle: resolve annexation before judging the host's definiteness

common_mistakes.pattern: prefixing the article to the comment of a noun-initial sentence
common_mistakes.why_wrong: matched definiteness cancels the assertion in the construction taught so far
common_mistakes.correction_principle: keep the comment indefinite until the constructions that license a definite comment have been learned

sarf_relevance: medium — the surface exponents at issue (article clitic, nunation, pronominal suffix) are morphological layering facts even though no derivation is taught
nahw_relevance: high — definiteness conditions slot selection, agreement inside noun phrases, and the licensing of several later constructions
tutor_drill_relevance: high — source attribution is a clean, checkable task, and the nunated proper name is an ideal item for eliciting the lesson's own weakest generalisation
rich_hover_relevance: very high — definiteness is a per-token property a hover layer must state, and the source of that definiteness is exactly the kind of justification a hover explanation needs
corpus_pvn_relevance: n entries dominate (common nouns, proper names, and annexed hosts); p entries cover the article clitic and the pronominal suffixes as definiteness sources; no v material; the salient candidate class for entry work is nunated proper names, which falsify the marker-based test
required_evidence: per occurrence: presence of the article, presence of nunation, annexation status and the definiteness of the second term, membership in a closed definite class, and proper-name status; a definiteness verdict must name its source, not merely its marker
uncertainty_flags: the enumeration of definiteness sources varies among standard grammars, some counting the determined vocative separately, so the count of six is one convention and must stay attributed
the claim that two definite slots cannot form a sentence conflicts with well-known definite-comment constructions and is flagged for review before any projection
the marker-based indefiniteness test contradicts the lesson's own use of nunated proper names as definite topics in earlier lessons of this module

proposed_new_units.summary: Licensing table mapping each source of definiteness (article, proper name, closed definite classes, annexation to a definite) to the surface evidence that establishes it and to the surface evidence that would otherwise be misleading, so that a definiteness verdict is issued by source rather than by marker.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers how clitics and inflectional layers stack on a surface but does not adjudicate definiteness, and u-n01 consumes definiteness without deriving it; nothing in the catalog blocks the nunation-means-indefinite inference that this lesson's own examples falsify.
